summary: ```markdown # AI Pose Generator | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, my name is Phoebe, and I'm going to go through our AI pose generator feature that's in beta right now. It came out in 2025.0, and it's a really cool feature because it will have Clo automatically generate poses for you based off of images. So let's dive on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Getting Started Okay, so here's my screen, and I have an outfit and an avatar all set up. Let's say I'm ready to start adding in poses. Of course, I can go to my library, which is now located at the top. I can navigate to "Avatar Female Poses" and bring in any of these poses for this person to change into. However, I can also use the AI pose generator. ### Locating the Feature So, where is this feature? It is at the very top toolbar. You can go to "Avatar," and then at the bottom, you'll see "AI Pose Generator" with a note that it's in beta. This just means we know it's not final; there are still some things to fix. However, we wanted to get this to you all as soon as possible so that you can start using it and provide as much feedback as you'd like for us to keep improving. ## Using the AI Pose Generator When you select the AI pose generator, a pop-up window will appear, informing you that everything in your window will be deleted and cleared out. It will notify you that the AI pose generator will delete all avatars and garments in the 3D window. Do you want to proceed? I’m going to hit cancel because I don't want this erased. ### Opening a New File You might be asking yourself, "Okay, Phoebe, then what do we do?" I'm going to open up a blank file and then go back to the AI pose generator beta. ## Generating Poses Now that we know where this feature is, let's figure out how it works. In the pop-up window for the AI pose generator, you can either generate an image to create your pose or drop in an image to generate a pose. First, I'll select the gender I want to use. The poses that you save and create can be used for both male and female avatars in Clo. ### Selecting an Avatar I’m just going to start with a female avatar. Upon selection, a mannequin-like avatar will appear, showing you previews of your different generated poses. If you like any of them, you can save them. ### Utilizing Text Prompts Let's quickly go through how this pop-up window works. After selecting my gender, I receive text prompts. I could quickly write a text prompt, for example, "jumping up," and then hit generate. This will generate an image. If I don't like the image, I can hit generate again, and another image will come up. ### Adjusting Poses If I like the pose but want to adjust it, I can move the avatar off the ground using the toggle menu. You can go to "Show Avatar Joints," with the shortcut being Shift + X. You can click at the middle and move things around. ### Saving Poses If I like this pose, I can hit save. Besides typing in a prompt, there are keyword suggestions available. You can select as many or as few as you want, but be mindful that you can only select two in each section. ### Understanding Pose Types For basic poses, options include running, standing, or walking. You can't run and stand simultaneously, nor can you stand and walk at the same time. For action and sports poses, you could be an archer jumping, playing basketball, or in a soccer game shooting a ball. ## Generating Images When you're satisfied with your selections, you can proceed to generate an image. You can also maintain the prompt and generate similar results by using the pin option. If the images generated do not meet your expectations, you can erase everything and restart. ### Random Prompt Option Another cool feature is the random prompt option, represented by a dice icon. Selecting this will create a random prompt for you. ### Reviewing Generated Images Every image created can be found in the history section. You can review all generated images and regenerate any if desired. Additionally, you can select multiple images and save them to your computer. ## Uploading Your Own Images If you prefer using your own photos, you can upload images directly. Ensure the images show the full body, are unobstructed, and have a clear background. Using actual people rather than animated characters will yield better results. ### Finalizing Your Poses Once you are happy with your poses, you can save them. All poses are automatically saved within your pose library, but you can also create a folder on your desktop to store them. ## Workflow Suggestions For an efficient workflow, create your garments first, then save. Open another Clo window to start creating poses. This way, you can maintain a library of poses ready for stylized or fitting scenarios. ## Conclusion Thank you all so much for watching! I hope you enjoyed the video and learned a lot. If you have any questions, use the comment section below, and one of us will get back to you. Thanks again for watching, don't forget to like and subscribe, and check out all of the great videos we have on our Clo channel. Keep having fun in Clo! ```
